title: SnapshotManifest
description: Immutable, write-once, hash-verifiable manifest of everything the production model knew at one point in time (one stage, one date). See docs/SNAPSHOT_ARCHITECTURE.md. A manifest never embeds bulky payloads itself -- it references (REFERENCED_IMMUTABLE) or points to a frozen copy (FROZEN_COPY) of each component via lib/edgelab/schema_v1/snapshot_component.schema.json.

snapshotId.description: sha1('snapshot', snapshotStage, snapshotDate, productionRunKey-or-empty) -- see lib/edgelab/ids.py:build_snapshot_id. Deterministic and write-once per (stage, date, productionRunKey): a second capture attempt for the same key must verify-and-no-op or fail loudly, never silently produce a second manifest. For PRE_GAME_DECISION, productionRunKey distinguishes separate production decision moments for the same date (lineup recheck, doubleheader, retry) -- see lib/edgelab/snapshot.py's module docstring 'SNAPSHOT IDENTITY' section.

captureMode.description: LIVE_CAPTURE: written by a production workflow at (or shortly after) the moment it describes. HISTORICAL_BACKFILL: written later by scripts/backfill_snapshots.py against already-archived artifacts -- structurally distinguishes a backfilled manifest from a contemporaneous production capture, so a reader can never confuse the two.

snapshotStage.description: PRE_GAME_DECISION: everything known before first pitch, when the production decision was made. POST_GAME_SETTLEMENT: outcomes/settlement/CLV, captured only after the fact, never merged back into a PRE_GAME_DECISION manifest. CLOSING_LINE: the finalized closing quote per market, derived from checkpoint=CLOSING observations once no earlier quote can still arrive.

snapshotDate.description: The slate date (YYYY-MM-DD) this snapshot describes -- not the wall-clock date it was captured on (POST_GAME_SETTLEMENT/CLOSING_LINE are captured the following day).

capturedAt.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp this manifest was written.

productionRunId.description: Auto-derived productionRunKey (see lib/edgelab/snapshot.py:_production_run_key) -- data/pipeline/<date>/recommendations.json's own meta.createdAt at the moment scripts/build_market_ledger.py wrote it. Distinguishes separate production runs for the same date. Null when no recommendations.json artifact exists yet, or for stages that are not run-keyed (POST_GAME_SETTLEMENT, CLOSING_LINE).

workflowRunId.description: GitHub Actions run_id (github.run_id) of the workflow invocation that created this snapshot, when running in Actions; null for local/manual runs.

productionCommitSha.description: The git commit SHA that produced this run's model/pricing/recommendation code, sourced ONLY from productionProvenance.commitSha when productionProvenance.status is CAPTURED -- see the Forward Replay Corpus and Production Provenance milestone (docs/PRODUCTION_PROVENANCE.md). Distinct from snapshotWriterCommitSha (the commit that wrote THIS manifest -- always the same value within one workflow run, but a semantically different claim) and from a replay's own candidateModelCommitSha (the commit that RE-EXECUTED this snapshot's inputs later, possibly a different checkout entirely). Null whenever productionProvenance.status is not CAPTURED -- never reconstructed from any other source.

productionProvenance.description: Full provenance record resolved from data/pipeline/<date>/provenance.json (written by scripts/capture_production_provenance.py, the first step fetch-slate.yml runs after checkout, before any model-execution step). See docs/PRODUCTION_PROVENANCE.md.

gitHeadShaAtCapture.description: Live `git rev-parse HEAD` at capture time -- informational only, never used for automated ambiguity decisions. See scripts/capture_production_provenance.py's module docstring.

workingTreeDirty.description: Whether CODE paths (scripts/, lib/, config/) had uncommitted changes at capture time -- True or null (unknown) both mean AMBIGUOUS, never treated as clean.

eventName.description: GITHUB_EVENT_NAME (e.g. 'schedule', 'workflow_dispatch', 'push') -- corpus-health audit (2026-08-25 follow-up): the ground-truth signal for whether this run's fetch-slate.yml execution had the risk-gate/execution chain available at all. See lib/edgelab/snapshot.py:is_schedule_triggered_run.

snapshotWriterCommitSha.description: git commit SHA of THIS repo checkout at the moment this manifest was written (same convention as lib/edgelab/model_evaluation.py's _git_commit_sha()). This is the snapshot-creation-time commit, not necessarily productionCommitSha.

modelVersion.description: No single global model/engine version exists in this repository today (confirmed: only f5PricingVersion is populated, for F5_ML_Away/Home rows). Always null at this schema version -- see pricingVersionsByFamily for the one real, populated version.

pricingVersionsByFamily.description: Map of market-family-name -> pricing/model version string, populated only for families that actually carry one today (e.g. {'F5_ML': 'f5_three_way_v1'}). Families with no versioning concept are simply absent, never given a fabricated value.

rulesConfigVersion.description: config/rules.json's own '_version' field at capture time, copied verbatim. NOT claimed to be the complete production rule set -- see the EFFECTIVE_CONFIG component and docs/SNAPSHOT_ARCHITECTURE.md's 'effective configuration' section for why rules.json alone is insufficient.

temporalConsistency.description: Workflow-run-skew check (see lib/edgelab/snapshot.py:detect_temporal_skew): compares every pipeline-stage artifact's own meta.createdAt against the productionRunId reference timestamp. skewDetected=true means this manifest's components may have been drawn from meaningfully different production runs -- forces completenessStatus to at most PARTIAL_REPLAY (see derive_completeness_status).

replayFidelityPotential.description: The BEST replay fidelity level this snapshot could support if consumed today, mechanically derived from component availability -- never a narrative judgment. See docs/SNAPSHOT_ARCHITECTURE.md.

completenessStatus.description: Mechanically derived from component availabilityStatus values, commit ambiguity, and temporal-skew detection -- see lib/edgelab/snapshot.py:derive_completeness_status's exact rule table, never assigned by narrative judgment. INTEGRITY_FAILURE is never written here by the builder (a failed freeze-time hash check aborts the build entirely) -- it is only ever produced by a READER re-verifying an already-stored manifest (see completeness_report()).

components.description: Every SnapshotComponent this stage assesses, including ones with availabilityStatus MISSING/NOT_APPLICABLE_FOR_STAGE -- a component that was never captured still gets an explicit entry, never a silent omission.

missingComponents.description: componentType values (from components) whose availabilityStatus is MISSING -- denormalized for fast lookup without scanning the full components array.

limitationReasons.description: Deduplicated union of every non-null component limitationReason, plus any stage-level limitation (e.g. POSTGAME_DATA_EXCLUDED_FROM_PREGAME_SNAPSHOT).

linkedSnapshotIds.description: snapshotId values of OTHER stage manifests for the same snapshotDate that this manifest links to (e.g. a POST_GAME_SETTLEMENT manifest links back to its PRE_GAME_DECISION snapshotId). The earlier-stage manifest is never mutated to add a forward link -- only later manifests carry a linkedSnapshotIds pointer backward.

manifestHash.description: SHA-256 of this manifest's own canonical, content-only serialization (sorted keys; capturedAt/workflowRunId/snapshotWriterCommitSha/provenance/manifestHash itself excluded -- those are 'when/how captured' facts, not 'what was captured'. productionRunId IS included -- it is part of WHAT was captured, since it identifies which production run's artifacts were frozen). Proves the captured DATA has not changed since creation -- see lib/edgelab/snapshot.py:compute_manifest_hash.
